ing: scotch bonnet or other hot chili
st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt, half the ginger, and half the garlic. Brown in [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot for 5 minutes per side, then set aside.
Blend the tomatoes, bell peppers, chili, and the chopped onion into a smooth puree.
Add [[0.5 cup]] oil to the pot, cook the sliced onion for 5 minutes, then stir in [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste for 3 minutes.
Pour in the puree and cook on medium for 25 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil separates.
Stir in the remaining ginger and garlic, [[1 tsp]] curry powder, [[1 tsp]] thyme, bay leaves, and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add [[3 cups]] broth and the chicken. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check that the chicken is at 165°F (74°C), fluff the rice, and serve hot.

ing: or 2 tbsp baking soda plus 1 tsp paprika for color
st: Soak the black-eyed peas in water overnight, or boil for 2 minutes and soak for 1 hour. Drain.
Put the peas in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and the sorghum leaves. Boil for 40 minutes until the peas are nearly soft and the water is deep red-brown.
Remove and discard the leaves, leaving the colored cooking water.
Stir the rinsed rice and [[1.5 tsp]] salt into the pot, making sure the water covers the rice by 1 inch. Add water if needed.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, and peel. Cook the spaghetti in salted water and drain.
Fry the fish in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through.
Serve the rice and beans with eggs, spaghetti, fish, and shito on the side.

ing: scotch bonnet or other hot chili
st: Put the chicken in a pot with [[6 cups]] water, half the onion, the ginger, the garlic, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, remaining onion, and the chili into a puree.
Add the puree to the pot and simmer, partly covered, for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the soup is red-orange.
Meanwhile, cut the cassava into chunks, removing the woody core, and cut the plantains. Boil together in water for 25 minutes until very soft.
Drain, then pound in a mortar or mash in a food processor, adding splashes of hot water, until smooth and stretchy.
With wet hands, shape the dough into 6 smooth balls.
Taste the soup, add [[0.5 tsp]] salt if needed, and ladle into bowls with the fufu in the center.

ing: or 2 cups cornmeal fermented 2 days with water
or cassava flour mixed with water
st: Score the tilapia on both sides. Rub with [[1 tsp]] salt, the ginger, and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Blend or pound the chilies, onion, tomatoes, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a coarse, fresh pepper sauce.
Grill or broil the fish for 8 minutes per side until the flesh flakes and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Mix the corn dough and cassava dough in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and stir out the lumps. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Cook for 10 minutes as it thickens, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cover and steam on low for 10 minutes, then stir and beat the dough against the side of the pot until smooth and stretchy.
With a wet bowl, shape the banku into 4 smooth balls.
Serve with the grilled tilapia and the pepper sauce.

ing: or cornmeal soured with water for 2 days
small whole fish such as tilapia
st: Soak the corn husks in warm water for 20 minutes. If using foil, cut 12 pieces about 10 inches square.
Put half the corn dough in a pot with [[1.5 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring hard, until it forms a thick sticky paste.
Cool the paste for 10 minutes, then knead it into the other half of the raw dough.
Divide into 6 balls. Wrap each ball tightly in 2 layers of husks, tying them closed with strips of husk or string.
Place the wrapped balls in a pot with [[1.5 cups]] water in the bottom. Cover and boil gently for 2 hours, adding water if needed.
Meanwhile, season the fish with salt and fry it in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 5 minutes per side, until crisp and cooked through.
Blend the chilies, onion, and tomatoes into a rough sauce.
Unwrap the kenkey and serve with the fried fish and pepper sauce.

ing: scotch bonnet or other hot chili
st: Soak the black-eyed peas overnight in water, or boil for 2 minutes and soak for 1 hour. Drain.
Cover the peas with [[5 cups]] fresh water in a pot, bring to a boil, and simmer for 40 minutes until soft.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] palm oil in a skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the ginger, tomatoes, and chili, cooking for 10 minutes until jammy.
Add the tomato mixture to the beans with [[1 tsp]] salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] vegetable oil in a skillet. Fry the plantains for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and caramelized. Drain.
Sprinkle the plantains with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and serve alongside the beans.
Peel the plantains and cut them into 1-inch cubes.
Mix the ginger, garlic, [[1 tsp]] cayenne, cloves, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl with a splash of water to make a paste.
Toss the plantain cubes in the paste until all are coated. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the cubes in batches for 4 minutes, turning, until dark golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain the fried plantain cubes on a plate lined with paper towels.
Serve hot, plain or with roasted peanuts.

ing: scotch bonnet or other hot chili
st: Put the chicken in a large pot with [[6 cups]] water, half the onion, the ginger, the garlic, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, the remaining onion, and the chili until smooth. Add it to the pot with [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste.
Let the soup simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Whisk [[1 cup]] peanut butter with [[1 cup]] of the hot broth in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the peanut mixture into the pot, stirring well. Simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the oil rises to the top.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C), taste, and add [[0.5 tsp]] salt if needed. Serve with rice balls or fufu.

ing: scotch bonnet or other hot chili
st: Wash and chop the spinach.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] palm oil in a pot over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, ginger, and chili and cook for 8 minutes until broken down.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] ground egusi with [[0.25 cup]] water into a paste, then spoon small lumps into the pot.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes without stirring, until the egusi sets into curds.
Add the fish, [[0.75 cup]] water, and [[1 tsp]] salt and stir gently.
Add the spinach and fold it in. Cover and cook for 15 minutes until soft and rich in color.
Taste for salt and serve with yam, rice, or kenkey.
Blend the onion, garlic, ginger, and chilies into a thick paste, adding a splash of water if the blades stick.
Grind the dried shrimp and flake the dried fish finely.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the onion paste and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until most of the water cooks off.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and the bay leaf and cook for 5 minutes until the oil turns red.
Stir in the shrimp, fish, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook on low for 25 minutes, stirring, until dark brown and oily.
Cool fully, remove the bay leaf, and spoon into clean jars. Keep in the fridge for up to 1 month.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1.25 cups]] warm water gradually and beat for 3 minutes into a thick, sticky batter.
Cover and let the batter rise in a warm place for 60 minutes until doubled and bubbly.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a heavy pot at least 3 inches deep to 350°F (175°C).
Scoop a ball of batter with a wet spoon or wet hand and drop it carefully into the oil. Fry in small batches.
Fry for 4 minutes, turning, until puffed and deep golden all over.
Drain on paper towels and let cool for 5 minutes before eating warm.
